definitions.explanation: A feeling that something is about to happen, without having concrete evidence. Can be about both good and bad events.

examples.japanese: {嫌|いや}な{予感|よかん}がする。
examples.english: I have a bad feeling about this.

examples.japanese: {何|なに}かいいことが{起|お}きる{予感|よかん}がした。
examples.english: I had a feeling something good was going to happen.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}から{嫌|いや}な{予感|よかん}がしていたが、やはり{試験|しけん}の{結果|けっか}は{悪|わる}かった。
examples.english: I had a bad feeling since morning, and sure enough, the exam results were poor.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {予感|よかん}がする (to have a premonition)
- {嫌|いや}な{予感|よかん} (a bad feeling)
- {予感|よかん}が{的中|てきちゅう}する (a premonition comes true)
- {予感|よかん}が{当|あ}たる (a hunch proves right)

The phrase {嫌|いや}な{予感|よかん}がする is extremely common and is often the first thing that comes to mind when Japanese speakers sense something will go wrong.
